   188	// nativeWriteHookSpec builds the PreToolUse hook entry that intercepts
   189	// nativeWriteTools before agy executes them. See nativeWriteHookCommand for
   190	// the allow/deny logic. Verified live against agy 1.1.15: a call targeting
   191	// a path inside the conversation's real artifactDirectoryPath is allowed
   192	// and the physical write lands there; a call targeting a workspace path is
   193	// denied before it ever reaches the filesystem.
   194	func nativeWriteHookSpec() hookSpec {
   195		return hookSpec{
   196			PreToolUse: []hookGroup{
   197				{
   198					Matcher: strings.Join(nativeWriteTools, "|"),
   199					Hooks:   []hookHandler{{Command: nativeWriteHookCommand(), Timeout: 5}},
   200				},
   201			},
   202		}
   203	}

   205	// ensureNativeWriteHook idempotently provisions Tractor's PreToolUse
   206	// allow/deny hook under homeDir's global agy hooks.json, merging with (not
   207	// replacing) any other hooks already configured there.
   208	//
   209	// Global placement is deliberate, unlike a workspace-local
   210	// .agents/hooks.json: Tractor's isolated-worktree branches (engine/artifacts.go,
   211	// added in 2485e4c) each get their own workdir, so a workspace-local hook
   212	// would need provisioning into and cleanup from every branch worktree, and
   213	// a leftover file would show up in that branch's git status and risk being
   214	// swept into artifact collection — exactly what this fix must not do. A
   215	// single global hooks.json, provisioned once, avoids both problems. It also
   216	// affects the user's own manual interactive agy sessions sharing the same
   217	// global config; because the policy is artifact-aware (allows genuine
   218	// in-brain artifact writes, only denies workspace-targeted ones), it does
   219	// not break that usage the way an unconditional deny would.
   220	//
   221	// The read-modify-write is guarded by an exclusive flock on a sibling lock
   222	// file, and the write itself lands via a same-directory temp file plus
   223	// rename, so two concurrent Tractor processes (or a person editing
   224	// hooks.json by hand) cannot lose each other's keys or observe a
   225	// partially-written file.
   226	func ensureNativeWriteHook(homeDir string) error {
   227		dir := filepath.Join(homeDir, ".gemini", "config")
   228		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
   229			return fmt.Errorf("create %s: %w", dir, err)
   230		}
   231	
   232		unlock, err := lockHooksConfig(homeDir)
   233		if err != nil {
   234			return err
   235		}
   236		defer unlock()
   237	
   238		path := hooksConfigPath(homeDir)
   239		canonical, err := json.Marshal(nativeWriteHookSpec())
   240		if err != nil {
   241			return fmt.Errorf("encode tractor native-write hook: %w", err)
   242		}
   243	
   244		raw, readErr := os.ReadFile(path)
   245		doc := map[string]json.RawMessage{}
   246		switch {
   247		case readErr == nil:
   248			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &doc); err != nil {
   249				return fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w (fix or remove the file so Tractor can add its hook)", path, err)
   250			}
   251		case os.IsNotExist(readErr):
   252			// doc stays empty; created below.
   253		default:
   254			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, readErr)
   255		}
   256	
   257		if existing, ok := doc[tractorHookName]; ok {
   258			if bytes.Equal(bytes.TrimSpace(existing), canonical) {
   259				return nil
   260			}
   261			if !strings.Contains(string(existing), nativeWriteHookMarker) {
   262				return fmt.Errorf(
   263					"%s already has a %q hook that is not Tractor-managed (missing marker comment in its reason text); "+
   264						"remove it or rename Tractor's hook (harness/agy.tractorHookName) to avoid clobbering it",
   265					path, tractorHookName,
   266				)
   267			}
   268			// A stale Tractor-authored entry (e.g. an older reason string);
   269			// fall through and overwrite it with current content.
   270		}
   271	
   272		doc[tractorHookName] = canonical
   273		encoded, err := json.MarshalIndent(doc, "", "  ")
   274		if err != nil {
   275			return fmt.Errorf("encode %s: %w", path, err)
   276		}
   277		return writeFileAtomic(path, append(encoded, '\n'), 0o644)
   278	}
   279	
   280	// lockHooksConfig acquires an exclusive interprocess lock over homeDir's
   281	// hooks.json so two concurrent processes (two Tractor runs, or a person
   282	// editing the file by hand at the same moment) can't both read the same
   283	// old document and have the second writer silently discard the first
   284	// writer's new keys. Returns an unlock function; the caller must always
   285	// call it (e.g. via defer).
   286	func lockHooksConfig(homeDir string) (func(), error) {
   287		path := hooksLockPath(homeDir)
   288		file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o644)
   289		if err != nil {
   290			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", path, err)
   291		}
   292		if err := unix.Flock(int(file.Fd()), unix.LOCK_EX); err != nil {
   293			_ = file.Close()
   294			return nil, fmt.Errorf("lock %s: %w", path, err)
   295		}
   296		return func() {
   297			_ = unix.Flock(int(file.Fd()), unix.LOCK_UN)
   298			_ = file.Close()
   299		}, nil
   300	}
   301	
   302	// writeFileAtomic writes data to path via a same-directory temp file plus
   303	// rename, so a reader (or a process crash mid-write) never observes a
   304	// truncated or partially-written hooks.json. Rename within the same
   305	// directory is atomic on the POSIX filesystems agy's config lives on.
   306	func writeFileAtomic(path string, data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error {
   307		dir := filepath.Dir(path)
   308		temp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, filepath.Base(path)+".tmp-*")
   309		if err != nil {
   310			return fmt.Errorf("create temp file in %s: %w", dir, err)
   311		}
   312		tempName := temp.Name()
   313		defer func() { _ = os.Remove(tempName) }() // no-op once renamed away
   314	
   315		if _, err := temp.Write(data); err != nil {
   316			_ = temp.Close()
   317			return fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", tempName, err)
   318		}
   319		if err := temp.Chmod(perm); err != nil {
   320			_ = temp.Close()
   321			return fmt.Errorf("chmod %s: %w", tempName, err)
   322		}
   323		if err := temp.Sync(); err != nil {
   324			_ = temp.Close()
   325			return fmt.Errorf("sync %s: %w", tempName, err)
   326		}
   327		if err := temp.Close(); err != nil {
   328			return fmt.Errorf("close %s: %w", tempName, err)
   329		}
   330		if err := os.Rename(tempName, path); err != nil {
   331			return fmt.Errorf("rename %s to %s: %w", tempName, path, err)
   332		}
   333		return nil
   334	}

    90	func TestAgyVersionAtLeast(t *testing.T) {
    91		for _, tc := range []struct {
    92			actual, min string
    93			want        bool
    94		}{
    95			{"1.1.15", "1.1.15", true},
    96			{"1.1.16", "1.1.15", true},
    97			{"1.2.0", "1.1.15", true},
    98			{"2.0.0", "1.1.15", true},

   101			{"1.10.0", "1.9.0", true}, // numeric, not lexicographic, comparison
   102			{"1.1", "1.1.15", false},  // shorter actual treated as zero-padded
   103			{"1.1.15.2", "1.1.15", true},
   104		} {
   105			got, err := agyVersionAtLeast(tc.actual, tc.min)
   106			if err != nil {
   107				t.Fatalf("agyVersionAtLeast(%q, %q) unexpected error: %v", tc.actual, tc.min, err)
   108			}
   109			if got != tc.want {
   110				t.Errorf("agyVersionAtLeast(%q, %q) = %v, want %v", tc.actual, tc.min, got, tc.want)
   111			}

   115	func TestAgyVersionAtLeastRejectsUnparseableVersions(t *testing.T) {

   117			if _, err := agyVersionAtLeast(actual, minSupportedAgyVersion); err == nil {
   118				t.Errorf("agyVersionAtLeast(%q, ...) = nil error, want a parse error for an unparseable version", actual)
   119			}
   120		}
   121	}

   123	func TestEnsureNativeWriteHookConcurrentProvisioningLosesNoUpdates(t *testing.T) {
   124		home := t.TempDir()
   125		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(home, ".gemini", "config"), 0o755); err != nil {
   126			t.Fatal(err)
   127		}
   128	
   129		const otherWriters = 8
   130		var wg sync.WaitGroup
   131		errs := make(chan error, otherWriters+4)
   132	
   133		// Simulate other concurrent writers (other Tractor processes / tools)
   134		// each adding their own distinct top-level key via the same lock +
   135		// atomic-rename discipline ensureNativeWriteHook uses, racing against
   136		// several concurrent ensureNativeWriteHook calls.
   137		addForeignKey := func(name string) error {
   138			unlock, err := lockHooksConfig(home)
   139			if err != nil {
   140				return err
   141			}
   142			defer unlock()
   143			path := hooksConfigPath(home)
   144			doc := map[string]json.RawMessage{}
   145			if raw, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil {
   146				if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &doc); err != nil {
   147					return err
   148				}
   149			} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   150				return err
   151			}
   152			doc[name] = json.RawMessage(`{"PostToolUse":[]}`)
   153			encoded, err := json.MarshalIndent(doc, "", "  ")
   154			if err != nil {
   155				return err
   156			}
   157			return writeFileAtomic(path, append(encoded, '\n'), 0o644)
   158		}
   159	
   160		for i := 0; i < otherWriters; i++ {
   161			wg.Add(1)
   162			name := fmt.Sprintf("other-hook-%d", i)
   163			go func() {
   164				defer wg.Done()
   165				if err := addForeignKey(name); err != nil {
   166					errs <- err
   167				}
   168			}()
   169		}
   170		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
   171			wg.Add(1)
   172			go func() {
   173				defer wg.Done()
   174				if err := ensureNativeWriteHook(home); err != nil {
   175					errs <- err
   176				}
   177			}()
   178		}
   179		wg.Wait()
   180		close(errs)
   181		for err := range errs {
   182			t.Fatalf("concurrent provisioning error: %v", err)
   183		}
   184	
   185		raw, err := os.ReadFile(hooksConfigPath(home))
   186		if err != nil {
   187			t.Fatal(err)
   188		}
   189		var doc map[string]json.RawMessage
   190		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &doc); err != nil {
   191			t.Fatalf("hooks.json is not valid JSON after concurrent writers: %v (%s)", err, raw)
   192		}
   193		if _, ok := doc[tractorHookName]; !ok {
   194			t.Fatalf("tractor hook missing after concurrent provisioning: %s", raw)
   195		}
   196		for i := 0; i < otherWriters; i++ {
   197			name := fmt.Sprintf("other-hook-%d", i)
   198			if _, ok := doc[name]; !ok {
   199				t.Fatalf("concurrent writer's key %q was lost (read-modify-write race): %s", name, raw)
   200			}
   201		}
   202	}

1	# agy artifact-path bug: preventive layer (round 2 — rework)
     2	
     3	## TL;DR
     4	
     5	Round 1 shipped a global `PreToolUse` hook that **unconditionally** denied
     6	agy's three native write tools. Independent review correctly found this
     7	breaks legitimate native writes of real conversation artifacts (plans,
     8	walkthroughs, task files) for any `agy` session sharing the same global
     9	config, Tractor-launched or not — the hook never looked at *where* the
    10	write was targeted. This round rewrites the hook to be **artifact-aware**:
    11	it inspects the `PreToolUse` payload agy actually sends (captured live,
    12	not assumed) and allows a native write through when its target is
    13	genuinely inside the conversation's artifact directory, denying it only
    14	when the target lies outside — which is exactly the condition that
    15	triggers agy's own bug. It also fixes two structural gaps (no runtime
    16	invariant confirming the hook mechanism is supported; a non-atomic,
    17	unlocked global-file write vulnerable to concurrent processes) and — while
    18	proving the allow/deny behavior live — surfaced a new, more consequential
    19	agy defect that changes how much confidence to place in the existing
    20	repair-retry. Full reasoning and all live evidence:
    21	`ephemeral/worklog/202608191900-agy-artifact-prevention.md` (durable,
    22	survives the source research reports being deleted).
    23	
    24	## How each `EVAL_FEEDBACK.md` finding was addressed
    25	
    26	**1. Critical — unconditional deny hook breaks legitimate artifact
    27	writes.** Rewrote `nativeWriteHookCommand` (`harness/agy/native_write_hook.go`)
    28	to parse the hook's real stdin payload (`artifactDirectoryPath`, and every
    29	`TargetFile` under `toolCall.args`) and allow only when every extracted
    30	target lies under the artifact directory; deny (fail closed) otherwise,
    31	including when the payload doesn't parse as expected. Added unit tests for
    32	both decisions (`TestNativeWriteHookCommandAllowsInBrainTarget`,
    33	`TestNativeWriteHookCommandDeniesWorkspaceTarget`, plus edge cases for a
    34	missing artifact directory, an empty payload, and a call with more than one
    35	target) and live evidence with the *actual* Go-generated hook against real
    36	agy 1.1.15: an in-brain `write_to_file` call is allowed through, executes
    37	(`step_update.state: "DONE"`), and the file lands on disk with the right
    38	content; a workspace-targeted call is denied before touching disk. See
    39	"Smoke-test evidence" below and the worklog's "Live evidence" section for
    40	full transcripts.
    41	
    42	**2. Issue — no runtime invariant for the chosen prevention path.** The
    43	`--agent`/manifest/`init.tools` path stays abandoned (round 1's live
    44	evidence that agy 1.1.15 doesn't honor a mainAgent's `tools:` allowlist at
    45	all is unchanged and still holds — re-litigating it wasn't useful). What
    46	this round adds is the invariant the finding actually asked for on the
    47	**hook** path, which is what's shipped: `Adapter.ensureHook` now runs
    48	`agy --version` (cheap, no model turn) and fails the adapter fast,
    49	*before* touching `hooks.json`, if the installed agy is older than
    50	`minSupportedAgyVersion` (`1.1.15`, the only version this hook was
    51	verified live against) or reports an unparseable version string. This
    52	replaces "write the hook and hope" with an explicit, actionable,
    53	version-aware check. Tests:
    54	`TestEnsureHookFailsFastOnOldAgyVersion`,
    55	`TestEnsureHookFailsFastOnUnparseableAgyVersion`,
    56	`TestAgyVersionAtLeast` (+ rejection cases).
    57	
    58	**3. Issue — unlocked, non-atomic global config write.** `ensureNativeWriteHook`
    59	now acquires an exclusive `flock` (`golang.org/x/sys/unix`, already an
    60	indirect dependency, promoted to direct) on a sibling `.tractor-hooks.lock`
    61	file for the whole read-modify-write, and writes via a same-directory temp
    62	file plus `os.Rename` (atomic on the POSIX filesystems agy's config lives
    63	on) instead of `os.WriteFile` directly to the target path. A crash mid-write
    64	now orphans a harmless temp file instead of truncating `hooks.json`,  and
    65	two concurrent writers can no longer silently drop each other's keys.
    66	Test: `TestEnsureNativeWriteHookConcurrentProvisioningLosesNoUpdates` — several
    67	goroutines call `ensureNativeWriteHook` while several more each add a
    68	distinct foreign key via the identical lock-then-atomic-rename discipline;
    69	asserts every writer's key survives. Passes under `go test -race`.
    70	
    71	**4. Issue — worklog omitted the artifact-aware alternative and overstated
    72	net-positive.** Rewrote
    73	`ephemeral/worklog/202608191900-agy-artifact-prevention.md` in place: the
    74	hook design section now documents the artifact-aware mechanism (not the
    75	blanket deny), the real payload shape and `TargetFile` field name captured
    76	live, and both the allow and deny live proofs. Removed the round-1 framing
    77	that called the global blanket deny "net-positive" for interactive users —
    78	that claim depended on the exact behavior this round replaced. Also added,
    79	because it surfaced while gathering the live evidence this finding asked
    80	for: a newly discovered agy defect (conversation-level `result.status`
    81	appears to stick at `"ERROR"` across resumed turns after any hook denial,
    82	even when the resumed turn's own actions succeed or use no tools) that
    83	casts real doubt on whether the existing `ae5edb6` repair-retry can
    84	actually recover a turn against real agy. This wasn't asked for by the
    85	finding directly, but burying it would have repeated exactly the kind of
    86	unsubstantiated-optimism problem the finding was about — see the worklog's
    87	"The sticky conversation-status defect" section for full detail and the
    88	new Bug 3 upstream report.
    89	
    90	## What changed since round 1
    91	
    92	- `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go`: `nativeWriteHookCommand` rewritten
    93	  from an unconditional deny to an artifact-aware allow/deny (parses
    94	  `artifactDirectoryPath` + `TargetFile` from the real stdin payload, plain
    95	  POSIX `sh`/`sed`/`grep`, no `jq`/`python3` dependency). `ensureNativeWriteHook`
    96	  rewritten to use `lockHooksConfig` (flock) + `writeFileAtomic`
    97	  (temp-file/rename) instead of a bare `os.WriteFile`. Added
    98	  `minSupportedAgyVersion` and `agyVersionAtLeast`.
    99	- `harness/agy/adapter.go`: `ensureHook` now calls the new
   100	  `verifyAgyHookSupport` (runs `agy --version`, gates on
   101	  `minSupportedAgyVersion`) before provisioning the hook, inside the same
   102	  `sync.Once`. No other adapter logic changed — the `ae5edb6` repair-retry
   103	  is untouched, as instructed.
   104	- `harness/agy/adapter_test.go`: `TestAgyHelperProcess` now handles
   105	  `--version` (returns `AGY_HELPER_VERSION`, default `"1.1.15"`, without
   106	  polluting the invocation-count record other tests assert on). Added
   107	  `TestEnsureHookFailsFastOnOldAgyVersion`,
   108	  `TestEnsureHookFailsFastOnUnparseableAgyVersion`.
   109	- `harness/agy/native_write_hook_test.go` (new): hook-decision tests
   110	  (allow/deny/edge cases, run against the real `sh -c` command exactly as
   111	  agy invokes it), `agyVersionAtLeast` unit tests, and the concurrent
   112	  provisioning test.
   113	- `go.mod`: `golang.org/x/sys` promoted from indirect to direct (used for
   114	  `unix.Flock`). No new module downloaded — already present in the module
   115	  cache as a transitive dependency; `go.sum` unchanged.
   116	- `ephemeral/worklog/202608191900-agy-artifact-prevention.md`: rewritten
   117	  in place (see finding 4 above and "What I deliberately did NOT
   118	  re-litigate" below).
   119	
   120	## What I deliberately did NOT re-litigate
   121	
   122	The `--agent`/custom-agent-manifest/`init.tools` path from the original
   123	task spec: round 1's live evidence that agy 1.1.15 ignores a
   124	`--agent`-selected mainAgent's `tools:` allowlist entirely was not
   125	challenged by the eval and re-running those experiments would not have
   126	produced new information. That evidence, and the manifest shape kept for
   127	future reference, is preserved unchanged in the worklog.
   128

     1	# Evaluation feedback
     2	
     3	1. **Critical — the global hook disables valid Antigravity artifact writes outside Tractor.** `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:71-95` discards the hook payload and unconditionally denies all three native writers, while `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:98-112` installs that policy in the user's global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` and explicitly treats its effect on interactive sessions as a benefit. The primary research instead documents an artifact-aware policy (`deep-research-report-2.md:145-168`): allow targets under the hook payload's `artifactDirectoryPath` and deny targets outside it. The current policy therefore breaks legitimate writes to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/`, including normal implementation-plan, walkthrough, and task artifacts, for every manual agy session after Tractor runs. Rework the hook to inspect stdin and allow native writes whose target is contained within `artifactDirectoryPath`, while denying workspace/out-of-root targets. Add unit tests for both decisions and bounded live evidence proving an in-brain native write succeeds and an out-of-brain workspace write is denied. Do not claim global interactive benefit until both paths are demonstrated.
     4	
     5	2. **Issue — the delivered design omits the requested manifest, `--agent`, and `init.tools` fail-fast contract.** The invocation at `harness/agy/adapter.go:415-435` never passes `--agent`; the generated stream schema does not expose `init.tools`; and there is no enforcement that rejects advertised native writers or missing `run_command`. The recorded smoke evidence is convincing that agy 1.1.15 ignores a selected main agent's `tools:` allowlist: the selected agent still reports the same 57 tools, and a forced excluded `write_to_file` call executes and reproduces the artifact-path error. That is a valid reason not to ship a knowingly inert manifest, but it means the implementation no longer satisfies the explicit acceptance design and has no runtime invariant confirming that its replacement hook is supported or effective. Reconcile this explicitly in the implementation: either deliver the manifest/`--agent`/`init.tools` invariant on an empirically supported agy version, or make the hook fallback the accepted design and add an actionable, version-aware validation for that prevention path rather than silently trusting a written `hooks.json` entry.
     6	
     7	3. **Issue — global hook provisioning can clobber or corrupt user configuration under concurrency or interruption.** `ensureNativeWriteHook` performs an unlocked read-modify-write of the shared global file (`harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:120-156`), and `sync.Once` in `harness/agy/adapter.go:329-345` only serializes one Adapter instance. Two Tractor processes, or a user/configuration tool editing hooks concurrently, can both read the same old document and the last writer will discard the other's new keys. A process interruption during `os.WriteFile` can also leave the sole global hooks file truncated. If global placement remains, use interprocess coordination plus atomic same-directory temp-file/rename semantics (preserving appropriate permissions), and test concurrent merge behavior; otherwise choose a scoped placement that avoids shared persistent user state.

# Evaluation feedback

1. **Critical — the global hook disables valid Antigravity artifact writes outside Tractor.** `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:71-95` discards the hook payload and unconditionally denies all three native writers, while `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:98-112` installs that policy in the user's global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` and explicitly treats its effect on interactive sessions as a benefit. The primary research instead documents an artifact-aware policy (`deep-research-report-2.md:145-168`): allow targets under the hook payload's `artifactDirectoryPath` and deny targets outside it. The current policy therefore breaks legitimate writes to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/`, including normal implementation-plan, walkthrough, and task artifacts, for every manual agy session after Tractor runs. Rework the hook to inspect stdin and allow native writes whose target is contained within `artifactDirectoryPath`, while denying workspace/out-of-root targets. Add unit tests for both decisions and bounded live evidence proving an in-brain native write succeeds and an out-of-brain workspace write is denied. Do not claim global interactive benefit until both paths are demonstrated.

2. **Issue — the delivered design omits the requested manifest, `--agent`, and `init.tools` fail-fast contract.** The invocation at `harness/agy/adapter.go:415-435` never passes `--agent`; the generated stream schema does not expose `init.tools`; and there is no enforcement that rejects advertised native writers or missing `run_command`. The recorded smoke evidence is convincing that agy 1.1.15 ignores a selected main agent's `tools:` allowlist: the selected agent still reports the same 57 tools, and a forced excluded `write_to_file` call executes and reproduces the artifact-path error. That is a valid reason not to ship a knowingly inert manifest, but it means the implementation no longer satisfies the explicit acceptance design and has no runtime invariant confirming that its replacement hook is supported or effective. Reconcile this explicitly in the implementation: either deliver the manifest/`--agent`/`init.tools` invariant on an empirically supported agy version, or make the hook fallback the accepted design and add an actionable, version-aware validation for that prevention path rather than silently trusting a written `hooks.json` entry.

3. **Issue — global hook provisioning can clobber or corrupt user configuration under concurrency or interruption.** `ensureNativeWriteHook` performs an unlocked read-modify-write of the shared global file (`harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:120-156`), and `sync.Once` in `harness/agy/adapter.go:329-345` only serializes one Adapter instance. Two Tractor processes, or a user/configuration tool editing hooks concurrently, can both read the same old document and the last writer will discard the other's new keys. A process interruption during `os.WriteFile` can also leave the sole global hooks file truncated. If global placement remains, use interprocess coordination plus atomic same-directory temp-file/rename semantics (preserving appropriate permissions), and test concurrent merge behavior; otherwise choose a scoped placement that avoids shared persistent user state.

4. **Issue — the durable worklog omits the research's safer artifact-aware hook and preserves a false conclusion.** `ephemeral/worklog/202608191900-agy-artifact-prevention.md:204-239` describes only unconditional denial, and lines 258-269 call the global effect net-positive. Because the source reports are scheduled for deletion, this loses the material `artifactDirectoryPath` allow/deny alternative from `deep-research-report-2.md:145-168` and would steer future maintainers toward breaking legitimate brain-directory writes. Update both the worklog and `WORK_SUMMARY.md` to preserve the artifact-aware alternative, distinguish workspace-path failures from valid artifact writes, record the missing allow-case live evidence, and remove the unsupported net-positive claim.
